themes.name: Celts and Britons
themes.about: Before English there was Brittonic, the ancestor of Welsh, Cornish and Breton, spoken from Cornwall to the Clyde. Gaelic came to Scotland from Ireland.

themes.name: Romans
themes.about: From AD 43 to about 410 Britain was a Roman province, and its soldiers and settlers came from all over an empire that stretched from Syria to Spain.

themes.name: Anglo-Saxons
themes.about: Angles, Saxons and Jutes crossed the North Sea in the 400s and 500s. Their Old English is where English, and England, got their names.

themes.name: Norse and Vikings
themes.about: Raiders from the 790s, then settlers: farmers in the Danelaw, earls in Orkney and Shetland, traders who founded Dublin and Limerick.

themes.name: Normans
themes.about: Descendants of Vikings who settled in northern France and learnt French. They took England in 1066 and landed in Ireland in 1169. They left castles, and the word for pork.

themes.name: Huguenots
themes.about: French Protestants fleeing persecution, especially after 1685. They wove silk in Spitalfields and gave English the word refugee.

themes.name: Jewish communities
themes.about: Expelled from England in 1290, readmitted in 1656, and part of the life of these isles from Lincoln and York to Leeds, Manchester, Belfast and Dublin.

themes.name: The Irish abroad
themes.about: The Great Famine of 1845 to 1852 killed about a million people in Ireland and sent at least a million more abroad. Liverpool, Glasgow and America filled up with the Irish.

themes.name: Gypsies, Roma and Travellers
themes.about: Romani people, whose language comes from northern India, have been recorded in Britain since the early 1500s. Irish Travellers are a people of these isles too.

themes.name: Italian Scotland
themes.about: From the late 1800s Italians came to Scotland and opened cafes, ice-cream parlours and chip shops in nearly every town.

themes.name: Chinese Britain
themes.about: Chinese seamen settled in Liverpool from the 1860s, making its Chinatown one of the oldest Chinese communities in Europe.

themes.name: Black Britain
themes.about: There have been Black people in these isles since Roman times. Liverpool's Black community is among the oldest in Britain.

themes.name: Tiger Bay's seafarers
themes.about: Coal made Cardiff one of the world's great ports, and sailors from Somalia, Yemen, the Caribbean and everywhere else settled in Butetown.

themes.name: Windrush and Caribbean Britain
themes.about: In June 1948 the Empire Windrush docked at Tilbury. Its Caribbean passengers, and those who followed, helped rebuild Britain after the war.

themes.name: South Asian Britain
themes.about: Indian, Pakistani, Bangladeshi and Sri Lankan Britain goes back far further than the curry house, though it is fair to mention the curry house.

themes.name: Polish and Eastern European
themes.about: Polish airmen in the Battle of Britain, families who stayed after the war, and many more after 2004. Polish is now one of the most spoken languages in these isles.

themes.name: Ireland's new communities
themes.about: For centuries Ireland was a country people left. Since the 1990s it has been one people come to, from Brazil, Poland, India, Nigeria, Ukraine and more.
